requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: The full tree is owned by inventorysvc after repair and remains so after restart.

requirements.requirement: The inventory-readers group can read the existing data.
requirements.summary: Directories have group traversal and files have group-read permission; direct effective-GID tests successfully read both files before restart and a file afterward.

requirements.requirement: Users outside the owner and inventory-readers group cannot access the data.
requirements.summary: The tree has no permissions for others, and direct unrelated-user tests confirm both read and traversal denial, including after restart.
The same two files remain present, and their SHA-256 hashes exactly match the preparation baseline before repair, after repair, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 are unchanged. The repair used native platform account and permission utilities without installing or replacing software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: the pre-restart state was healthy, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and the system, identities, permissions, access behavior, and file hashes recovered. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot change and preserved platform health.
limitations: Requirement content_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the absent service account/group, changing ownership, and tightening modes directly implemented the requested outcome; the scheduled reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. Its transient harbor-node-reboot units did not remain after restart. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, new exposure, package damage, or abandoned temporary artifacts.
